newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, New Zealand to sign repo pact - Brash.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, New Zealand to sign repo pact - Brash.

text.p: New Zealand's Reserve Bank (RBNZ) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) will sign a bilateral repurchase (repo) pact on Wednesday, RBNZ governor Don Brash said on Tuesday.
Brash told Reuters that the agreement, allowing the RBNZ and the HKMA to aid each other in times of currency instability by improving market liquidity, followed an approach by Hong Kong.
"We will sign it tomorrow," Brash said at a meeting with Hong Kong business leaders, noting that the repo was New Zealand's first such deal.

The HKMA, Hong Kong's de facto central bank, has already signed repo agreements with the central banks of nine other Asian nations -- Australia, China, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea and Thailand.
The repo pacts are part of an effort among Asian countries to cooperate more in financial matters to avoid the type of crisis Mexico suffered in late 1994 when its currency came under attack.
